fixes.explanation: Gideon, Israel's leader in the fight with Midian, turns the throne down flat. He says, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son. The LORD shall rule over you.” That's a real answer. I can't even say no to a second cookie, and this man said no to a kingdom.

There's no short-term contract in his answer. Gideon says, “I will not rule over you…” and he says it flat out. The people offered rule to him, his son and his grandson. He answered that the LORD shall rule over them.

Gideon asks, and the Israelites answer, “We will give them gladly…” Then they spread out a garment, and each man throws an earring from his plunder onto it. Gladly, friend. I've seen people hold onto a cookie harder than that, and I was one of them.
Gideon places the ephod in Ophrah, his hometown. That's his own town, right where he lives. Hold on to that spot, because the verse tells us what happened there.
Shiloh is a good guess, friend, but this ephod never makes the trip. The text says Gideon placed it in Ophrah, his hometown. It stayed in his own town, and nobody had to pack a bag.
Bethel is a fair guess, but the text doesn't send the ephod there. It says Gideon placed it in Ophrah, his hometown. No road trip for this gold. It stays in Gideon's own town.

The text says the ephod “…became a snare to Gideon and his household.” A snare is a trap that catches you. All Israel ended up worshiping it there, and that's the trouble. Sometimes the thing that grabs your ankle is the one nobody saw coming.

The text doesn't say that. It says Gideon had seventy sons “…of his own, since he had many wives.” Those are his own sons, and the verse gives the reason right there. Boys from Midian never come up in it.

Nice try, friend, but his brothers' sons never show up in this verse. It says Gideon had seventy sons “…of his own, since he had many wives.” His own sons, and the verse hands us the reason. Seventy of them. I can barely keep track of one batch of cookies.
The text says, “…Gideon son of Joash died at a ripe old age…” He was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites. A long life, and he's buried in his father's tomb.

The text says, “…as soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned and prostituted themselves with the Baals…” The Baals were false gods. “As soon as” is the part that stings. Earlier the Israelites offered Gideon rule, and the moment he was gone they turned to the Baals.

That's not what the verse says. It says that as soon as Gideon was dead, “…the Israelites turned and prostituted themselves with the Baals…” Verse 35 adds that they did not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal. The passage never records anyone asking his sons to lead.
